text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — I’m planning a 12-week unpaid sabbatical starting May 3. Quick Q: what happens to my 401(k) employee deferrals, employer match, and vesting while I’m out? Can I make contributions directly or do a catch-up when I return? Also will HSA payroll contributions stop?

Jess Carter: Congrats on the sabbatical! Short answers: deferrals stop (no payroll), match pauses for unpaid periods, and vesting continues per schedule but check your service/vesting rules. HSA payroll contributions also stop. More details below. :sun_with_face:

Ben Patel: Adding payroll detail: our payroll system only withholds 401(k) deferrals on paid payruns. If you have no paycheck for a pay period, no deferral is taken, so no employer match is generated for that pay period.

Ben Patel: Vesting — continuous service counts toward vesting per the plan doc unless it's a LOA type that suspends service. For sabbaticals <12 weeks we usually treat it as continuous service, but confirm with People Ops if there are edge cases.

Alex Chen: OK — so no way to keep contributing while unpaid? I could do an after-tax transfer to the vendor?

Sam (Benefits Vendor): Hi Alex — Fidelity (our recordkeeper) can accept roll-ins and catch-up contributions after the fact in limited cases, but they cannot accept standard employee pre-tax deferrals outside of payroll withholding. Typical options:
- Make contributions via payroll when you return (catch-up via higher deferral if under IRS limits)
- If you have outside IRAs, consider a rollover later (not a contribution)

Sam (Benefits Vendor): If you want to explore an arranged ACH to the plan, that’s nonstandard and would need plan admin approval. Email benefits@redwood.com + copy me.

Jess Carter: Practical steps: 1) If you want to stop contributions, no action needed — payroll will stop automatically. 2) If you want to try to maintain savings rate post-leave, set a temporary higher deferral % to apply when you return (submit via Benefits Portal). 3) If you rely on HSA, consider pre-funding before leave — HSA contributions are year-based, but payroll HSA contributions stop with unpaid leave.

Ben Patel: For payroll reconciliation purposes, let us know your expected unpaid dates ASAP. If you want us to check vesting specifics, ping me with hire date and plan hire date and I’ll confirm.

Alex Chen: Thanks — hire date 2021-09-15. I’ll send calendar invite + official LOA request today. Would love confirmation on vesting.

Jess Carter: Got it. @Ben Patel can you confirm vesting for Alex?

Ben Patel: On it. I’ll run it with payroll and plan admin today.

hr-bot: Policy snippet (automated): "401(k) contributions are withheld from eligible payrolls. Employer match is calculated on eligible pay periods and is subject to plan vesting rules. Extended unpaid leaves may be treated as continuous service for vesting at plan discretion. Contact benefits@redwood.com for exceptions."

Ben Patel: Quick update — confirmed with plan admin: Alex’s continuous service will count toward vesting for a 12-week unpaid sabbatical, so no vesting interruption. Employer match will still be paused for pay periods with no deferrals. I sent a follow-up to Alex via email with the plan admin summary.

Alex Chen: Awesome, thanks everyone. One last Q — if I return mid-pay-period, does match prorate?

Sam (Benefits Vendor): Match is applied based on payroll period contributions. If you have a partial-period pay and a deferral is taken, the match for that pay will apply on that contribution. For prorating specifics we follow pay-period-based calculation, not calendar-day proration.

Jess Carter: TL;DR: vesting keeps going, contributions/match pause during unpaid, plan admin can advise on edge cases. Email benefits@redwood.com if you want us to request special arrangements. Enjoy the sabbatical! :beach_with_umbrella:
